chunks: Muawiya ibn 'Ammar narrated from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the man who performs Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa while riding. He said: 'There is no problem, and walking is superior.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'ee ritual
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / no harm (permissible)
key_terms.يَسْعَى: He runs/walks briskly (the specific action of Sa'ee)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to ride during Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that while riding between Safa and Marwa is legally valid (mubah), walking remains the preferred act of worship (afdhal), reflecting the principle of balancing ease with devotion. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Prophet's and Imams' practices while accommodating physical limitations, ensuring the ritual's accessibility without diminishing its spiritual merit.
